SYMPTOM: React compiler lint error when calling `setState` with functional updater inside `useEffect` (e.g. `setVisiblePtyIds(prev => ...)`) — even though functional updater reads `prev`, not stale state. Error from `eslint-config-next` / react-compiler plugin.
CAUSE: Next.js 16's built-in React compiler can't statically verify functional updaters in effects are safe — it rejects any setState call inside useEffect.
FIX: Replace `useState` + `useEffect` pattern with `useReducer` + `useEffect` dispatch. Define reducer with named actions (sync, show, hide, reorder, add). Effect dispatches `{ type: 'sync', ids: [...] }` instead of calling setState.
PREVENT: Any time you need to sync derived state from props/context in useEffect, use useReducer. useState in useEffect always fails React compiler check.
GOTCHA: `// eslint-disable-next-line react-compiler/react-compiler` won't work — the plugin isn't installed separately. `// eslint-disable-next-line` alone doesn't know the rule name. Only useReducer fully satisfies the compiler.
